text:
maria-support: Customer reported sudden 401s in prod after rotating API key via our CLI. They pasted the new key into their env var and started getting invalid_api_key. They say it worked locally for a minute then failed.

devon-eng: Can you paste the exact curl (redact full key) they used and how they copied the key?

maria-support: Customer says they used the macOS CLI flow and `pbcopy` — command sequence they gave: 
```
redwood keys create --label prod-2026-03 && redwood keys get --id <id> | pbcopy
export REDWOOD_KEY=$(pbpaste)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Api-Key $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/models
```
Response: `\{"error\":\"invalid_api_key\", \"message\":\"401 Unauthorized\"\}`. They pasted the key into a k8s secret manifest and then into a container env var.

maria-support: They pasted a debug echo for us (redacted) that showed: `abcd1234efgh5678\n` (note the literal backslash-n in their paste).

devon-eng: That looks like an escaped newline made literal (the CLI output probably had a trailing newline and an intermediate tool double-escaped it). Ask them to run `printf "%s" "$REDWOOD_KEY" | xxd` inside the container to show bytes. Also verify with `printf "%s" \"$REDWOOD_KEY\" | hexdump -C`.

maria-support: Customer ran `printf "%s" "$REDWOOD_KEY" | xxd` and pasted output: 
```
00000000: 6162 6364 3132 3334 6566 6768 3536 3738  abcd1234efgh5678
00000010: 5c 6e                                      \n
```
So there is an actual two-byte sequence 0x5c 0x6e (backslash + n) at the end, not a single 0x0a newline.

devon-eng: OK that explains it. Our auth check expects the raw 24/36/whatever-byte token; a literal backslash+n will change the HMAC/signature comparison. Two common causes: (1) some copy/paste/sanitizer replaced the actual newline with the two-character escape sequence when saving into the secret manifest (e.g., JSON/string quoting), or (2) the CLI printed an already-escaped representation and they piped that through another tool.

maria-support: Customer confirms they put the key into a YAML manifest as a quoted string like `apiKey: "abcd1234efgh5678\n"` because they thought the newline needed to be escaped.

devon-eng: Advise steps to fix: 1) Rotate the affected key (they should create a new key id) 2) When copying into manifests or env, avoid adding escape characters — use `printf "%s" "$KEY" > /tmp/key && cat -v /tmp/key` to validate no literal `\n` sequence. For k8s, use `stringData` with the raw value or `kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-file=key=/path/to/key`.

james-support: I sent the customer an example command to create a clean secret on Linux/mac: 
```
echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY" | base64 -w0 > redwood-key.b64
kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-literal=apiKey=$(echo -n "$REDWOOD_KEY")
```

infra-bot: Key id rkd_01A2B3C4 flagged: last attempted validation 2026-03-01T14:22:10Z returned invalid_api_key. Disabled pending rotation.

maria-support: Customer rotated and re-deployed with the new secret using `echo -n` -> base64 -> k8s secret. They confirm requests immediately started succeeding.

devon-eng: Root cause: escaped backslash-n characters present in stored secret (0x5c 0x6e) instead of real newline or no newline. We should add a short troubleshooting snippet to the CLI docs about copying keys into manifests (recommend `echo -n` / `printf` / `kubectl --from-file`) and call out common pitfalls with JSON/YAML quoting producing literal `\n`.

maria-support: Customer happy, marked resolved :white_check_mark: Closing thread.
